author: Thomas Lowson
title: The Undertaker Slams Attitude Era Angle - 'It Sucked, I Hated It' - NewsBreak
text:
By Thomas Lowson ,
1 hours ago
1999 saw The Corporation and the Ministry of Darkness merge on WWE TV to form the Corporate Ministry, though the group only lasted months.
The two groups officially merged during the pilot episode of WWE SmackDown in late April, but officially disbanded in early August, after just three months.
On a recent edition of his “Six Feet Under” podcast, The Undertaker spoke about the original Ministry, sharing his delight about the faction. He said,

READ MORE: Chelsea Green Is Dealing With PTSD
“The Ministry, that was a lot of fun. We really, really got to push the envelope with the Ministry, with the symbolism and all of the innuendo and everything else… That was some really, really cool stuff that we did. And the sacrifices and just the overall darkness of it really pushed a lot of people’s buttons.”
While the WWE icon loved his time with the Ministry, merging with The Corporation was a terrible idea as far as The Undertaker was concerned. He said,
“I think we had something that was really edgy and, again, made people think and made people feel a certain way. When it became the Corporate Ministry, it was just like, womp, womp, womp, womp, womp. Y eah, it sucked. It really did. I hated it.”
The Undertaker would vanish from TV shortly after the end of the Corporate Ministry, as he was going through a divorce and needed time off.
After missing WrestleMania, The Undertaker returned in mid-2000 at the Judgment Day pay-per-view event as the American Badass character.
